blocks.text: This step is about scale and UX safety: long conversations, large responses, and unreliable networks. Explain how you keep the chat fast and reliable over time.

Ship composition-safe input, recoverable drafts, attachment readiness, idempotent send, and honest Stop behavior first. Add virtualization or visual delta batching only after measuring current-turn and long-list costs.

Composer and current-turn resilience evidence:
- Long histories do not block the composer.
- Streaming does not trigger one framework commit per token.
- Stop, uncertain send, and retry converge by identity.
- Draft and attachment failures preserve recoverable user intent.

blocks.title: Composer performance controls
rows: Keeps scrolling smooth on long histories
Coalesce text paints according to measured cost
Avoids excessive renders without changing accepted sequence
Persist by account and conversation with explicit cleanup
Restores intent without leaking drafts across users

blocks.title: Measured optimizations
items: Batch streaming chunks before state updates.
Page or virtualize history without coupling it to composer state.
Use a product-defined overlap policy; never let a newer command receive an older stream's deltas.
Cache recent conversations for quick load.

blocks.title: Composer failure and recovery
items: History payloads that are too large to load.
Error states that lose the user's prompt.
Stop button that does not actually cancel.

blocks.title: Scenario: long history and interrupted stream

steps.title: 1. Very long conversation
steps.text: Load only the latest N messages, show a Load more button, and virtualize the list.

steps.title: 2. User sends a new prompt
steps.text: Abort any existing stream and start a new one to avoid overlap.

steps.title: 3. Stream hiccup
steps.text: Show a retry CTA and keep the partial response so the user does not lose progress.

items.label: Main metric
items.helperText: Streaming makes the UI feel instant.

blocks.title: Composer resilience invariant
blocks.text: A great chat UX is resilient: it streams smoothly, cancels reliably, and scales to long histories without slowing down.

blocks.title: Failure modes
rows: Keep in-memory text and show nonblocking recovery status.
Keep text and the failed attachment row with retry or remove.
One file does not erase the prompt.
Retry the same client message identity.
Resume by cursor or fetch the message snapshot.

blocks.text: The textarea has a persistent label and instructions for Enter versus modified Enter without overriding platform composition. Attachments expose name, phase, error, and remove control. Streaming deltas are not announced token by token; meaningful completion, failure, or stop state uses a concise polite message. Focus remains in the composer after ordinary send unless navigation requires otherwise.

Test IME composition, mobile keyboards, voice input, paste, long drafts, large text, RTL, attachment races, duplicate send, stream interruption, and route restoration. Track accidental empty sends, draft loss, duplicate messages, stop latency, attachment recovery, and input responsiveness.

blocks.title: Interview answer checkpoint
blocks.text: Before finishing, explain how AI Chat Text Area (ChatGPT-Style) assigns client state ownership, preserves ordering, recovers from failure, measures performance, and manages keyboard focus.
